prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key commitments and measures (≤500 words)

Overall approach
- Five national missions: economic growth; clean energy; safer communities; opportunity through education and skills; an NHS fit for the future.
- “First steps”: fiscal stability; 40,000 extra NHS appointments per week; Border Security Command; Great British Energy; anti-social behaviour crackdown; 6,500 additional teachers.
- Fiscal rules: current budget to balance and debt falling by year 5. No increases to National Insurance, Income Tax rates or VAT. Measures against avoidance; abolish non‑dom status; close carried‑interest loophole; tighten use of offshore trusts.

Economy and business
- Industrial strategy with a statutory Industrial Strategy Council.
- National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to crowd in private investment: ports (£1.8bn), gigafactories (£1.5bn), steel (£2.5bn), carbon capture (£1bn), green hydrogen (£0.5bn).
- Corporation tax capped at 25% for the Parliament; permanent full expensing; replace business rates in England.
- 10‑year infrastructure strategy; National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority; full gigabit and 5G by 2030.
- Transport: bring rail into public ownership as contracts expire via Great British Railways; empower bus franchising and allow municipal ownership; fix 1m potholes/year; restore 2030 ICE phase‑out date, expand charging, standardise used‑EV battery info.
- Housing: build 1.5m homes; mandatory targets; more planning officers (funded via higher non‑resident SDLT surcharge); brownfield first plus strategic “grey belt” releases; new towns; boost social and affordable homes; permanent mortgage guarantee scheme.
- Devolution: landmark legislation, Local Growth Plans, multi‑year council settlements.
- Immigration and skills: reduce net migration via reformed points‑based system; sector workforce and training plans; stronger MAC role; bar abusive employers.

Work and living standards
- New Deal for Working People: ban exploitative zero‑hours; end fire‑and‑rehire; day‑one rights (parental leave, sick pay, unfair dismissal); Single Enforcement Body; minimum wage remit to reflect cost of living and remove adult age bands.
- Renters: abolish Section 21; empower challenges to unfair rent rises; extend Awaab’s Law; leasehold reform and movement to commonhold; building safety action; homelessness strategy.

Energy, climate, environment
- Zero‑carbon electricity by 2030: double onshore wind; triple solar; quadruple offshore wind; invest in CCUS, hydrogen, marine; Energy Independence Act; extend life of existing nuclear, proceed with Hinkley and Sizewell C, support SMRs; maintain strategic gas reserve.
- North Sea: no new exploration licences; do not revoke existing; ban fracking and new coal.
- Windfall tax reforms; retain ESIM.
- Great British Energy (£8.3bn), headquartered in Scotland; Local Power Plan.
- Grid upgrade and tougher regulation; reduce standing charges.
- Warm Homes Plan: +£6.6bn for 5m upgrades; PRS minimum efficiency by 2030.
- Water: special measures for failing companies; automatic fines; block bonuses; criminal sanctions; independent outlet monitoring.
- Farming: 50% public procurement local or higher-standard; land-use framework; ELMS improvements; TB strategy without badger cull. Animal welfare bans (trail hunting, trophy imports, puppy smuggling/farming, snares).

Crime and justice
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee; anti‑social behaviour “Respect Orders”; tougher shoplifting response and specific offence for assaults on shopworkers.
- Knife crime: mandatory interventions; bans on specific blades; executive liability for illegal online sales; Young Futures hubs nationwide.
- Violence against women and girls: specialist police units and fast‑track courts; stalking and spiking measures; legal advocates for victims.
- Police standards: stronger HMICFRS powers; mandatory vetting; automatic suspensions for serious allegations.
- Courts, prisons, probation: more prosecutors; sentencing review; build prison places; reduce reoffending via work, housing, learning; probation governance review.
- Historical injustices: Hillsborough Law; Windrush Commissioner; action on public inquiries.

Education and childcare
- 3,000 school‑based nurseries; review parental leave; free primary breakfast clubs.
- 6,500 teachers; support staff negotiating body; leadership and inspection reforms; curriculum and assessment review; SEND inclusion; school mental‑health professionals.
- Skills: Skills England; devolved adult skills; Technical Excellence Colleges; replace Apprenticeship Levy with flexible Growth and Skills Levy; HE funding reform; creative industries plan; football regulator; ticket resale protections.

Health and social care
- 2m extra annual NHS appointments/scans/operations; shared waiting lists; use independent sector capacity; NHS workforce plan.
- Double CT/MRI scanners; New Hospitals Programme; NHS innovation/adoption strategy; enhanced NHS app.
- Primary care: more GPs; face‑to‑face guarantee; pharmacist prescribing; direct referrals; trial Neighbourhood Health Centres.
- Dentistry Rescue Plan: 700,000 urgent appointments; contract reform; supervised toothbrushing (ages 3–5).
- National Care Service with national standards; Fair Pay Agreement in adult social care; family visit rights.
- Mental health: 8,500 extra staff; Young Futures hubs; modernise Mental Health Act.
- Public health: smoke‑free generation; restrict child‑appeal vaping; junk‑food ad ban to children; under‑16 energy drink sales ban; online safety enhancements; gambling regulation; halve healthy life expectancy gap; HIV plan to end new cases by 2030.

Governance and foreign policy
- Ethics and Integrity Commission; limit MPs’ second jobs; Commons modernisation; Lords reforms (end hereditary peers, retirement at 80, participation rules) and consult on replacement.
- Votes at 16; improve voter registration; donation and foreign‑interference safeguards.
- Devolution reset; Council of the Nations and Regions; specific Scotland/Wales/NI measures; repeal and replace NI Legacy Act.
- Defence and security: NATO and nuclear deterrent; Strategic Defence Review; path to 2.5% GDP on defence; defence industrial strategy; Armed Forces Commissioner; scrap visa fees for qualifying non‑UK veterans; steadfast support for Ukraine; AUKUS; calibrated China policy.
- Europe: no return to SM/CU/FoM; deepen UK‑EU cooperation (veterinary agreement, MRAs, touring artists, security pact).
- Trade: targeted agreements (e.g., India), sectoral deals, WTO/CPTPP engagement; global minimum tax.
- International development: rebuild capability in FCDO; restore 0.7% when fiscal conditions allow; focus on poverty, debt, women and girls, conflict prevention, climate finance; Clean Power Alliance.
